speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the recent school incident allegedly involving an offensive weapon procured online (a) whether our current measures are sufficient to restrict juveniles' access to offensive weapons; and (b) over the last three years, what is the number of juveniles who are arrested for possession of offensive weapons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Persons who handle these weapons are subject to certain safety conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, sellers must maintain transaction records of such items and owners of such items must store them securely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In determining which items to include, we have to find an appropriate balance, as almost any item can be used as a weapon, including those used in daily life like kitchen knives and choppers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Highly dangerous items like guns and explosives must be tightly regulated as they can cause a lot of damage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For other mixed-use items like axes which have normal legitimate uses, we may want to impose some controls, but need to consider carefully exactly what, so that we do not over-regulate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: First, we clearly need to look at it from a demand and supply issue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: To tighten the supply of these offensive weapons, what are the age verification checks required of online and brick-and-mortar retailers?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Second, are there any plans for these retailers to have to report suspicious transactions?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is not different from what MAS does for suspicious transactions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Third, how would MHA be working with the Ministry of Education (MOE) to strengthen awareness of the dangers of offensive weapons and checks of offensive weapons in schools?

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: First of all, the question about tightening the supply and imposing an age verification for controlled weapons or even mixed-use items like purchase of axes and knives, this is something we will constantly review to assess the appropriate level of controls we want to impose, especially for mixed-use items like axes and parangs that have legitimate uses.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: On the one hand, we do not want to over-regulate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: As I mentioned earlier, even for nefarious purposes, actually, access to kitchen knives and choppers can become a form of weapon.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: We will share more details when we have them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: It is even harder, sometimes, for retailers, especially online retailers, to understand or to verify the intent and the purpose of the purchase of legitimate items that are used for legitimate reasons.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: So, again, we will have to find the right balance and not to over-regulate, and to also be practical about this whole issue, while we understand the need to ensure that access to weapons is controlled especially for young children.
